This bail application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2.
Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.225/2025 of Perinadu Police Station, Pathanamthitta District; registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The prosecution case is that, the father of the accused had created an equitable mortgage for availing a loan in connection with a chitty transaction and after the death of his father, accused sold the property without the consent of the de facto complainant and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely arrayed as an accused and has no involvement in the alleged crime.
It was further submitted that no sale has even taken place and what was entered into was only an agreeent for sale.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application and submitted BAIL APPL. NO. 5320 OF 2025 2025:KER:39363 that the allegations against the petitioner are serious in nature and custodial interrogation is essential.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The mortgage creates a charge on the property.
Even if the property is sold subsequently, the charge will subsist.
Merely because the petitioner sold the property; or an agreement for sale is executed even while the original title deed is with KSFE, the charge cannot be affected.

Though the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that no sale has even taken place and all what was entered into was only an agreement for sale, the same need not be considered at this juncture.
Since KSFE is the de facto complainant, I am of the view that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1], it was held that, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant,
and the facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed are all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.

9. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would BAIL APPL. NO.
5320 OF 2025 2025:KER:39363 have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.

10. On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this Court is of the view that though the allegations are serious in nature, custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not required.
Further, having read to the nature of the offence and the severity of punishment,this Court is of the view that petitioner is entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.

11. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) In the event of the petitioner being arrested in Crime No.225/2025 of Perinadu Police Station, Pathanamthitta District, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation if he is so required in writing and shall co-operate with the investigation.
(c) Petitioner shall not destroy or tamper with the evidence or intimidate or threaten or contact the defacto complainant.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any other similar offences while he is on bail.
